insights.summary: At Arihant's Bharat Connect conference in March 2026, Prizor said it is on track for 7-8 lakh CCTV cameras in FY26 and wants to sell 1 crore a year by 2030-31, against an Indian market of 5-6 crore cameras growing about 20% a year. The plant runs at only 15-20% utilisation, new assembly lines cost under ₹1 Cr each, and the company has committed to buy 50 lakh made-in-India SoC chips a year from FY28 through its IndieSemic tie-up. No revenue or margin targets were given; prices are 10-15% below rivals, with a 10-15% hike taken in H2 FY26.

what_changed.text: Volume guidance of 7-8 lakh cameras for FY26 and a 1 crore cameras target by 2030-31
Commitment to buy 50 lakh SoC units a year from FY28 for three years
10-15% price hike in H2 FY26 on higher lens and SoC costs

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: Ground demand strong; sales growth via network expansion and compliance advantage

analyst_questions.answer: Utilisation is 15-20%; lines can be added for under ₹1 Cr each, with room for 4-5 lines in the current space.
About 20% of components still come from China, none security-critical; PCBs and housings are made in-house.
No revenue or margin targets were shared.

red_flags.text: A 50 lakh SoC units a year purchase commitment from FY28 is several times current volumes (7-8 lakh cameras); it is a large fixed obligation if demand falls short.
Competes on price (10-15% below rivals) in the price-sensitive segment, which limits margin room.
These are third-party notes, not a company transcript; wording is the note-takers', not management's.
